method: Same-agent English/Marathi block-by-block close reading, theory-by-theory reconstruction of every displayed axiom set, replay of the Russell-comprehension contradiction and mereological least-upper-bound clause, and exact formula, macro, controlled-token, identifier and reference comparison. No independent human or native-speaker review is claimed.
scope: Examples of first-order theories: strict linear orders, groups, Peano arithmetic, pure sets with unrestricted comprehension, and mereology.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Strict linear orders are axiomatized by irreflexivity, trichotomy with equality and transitivity, and the resulting structures are exactly the intended orders. Groups are axiomatized in a language with identity and a binary operation by right identity, associativity and right inverses.
samples.checks: Both language signatures, every displayed formula, the two directions of the order-model claim and all three group axioms are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Peano arithmetic receives successor, zero, addition, multiplication and order axioms, together with every instance of the induction schema. The system is infinite, the full schema is more complicated than shown, and the last displayed order axiom explicitly defines less-than.
samples.checks: All seven fixed axioms, the schema formula, infinitude reason, qualification and explicit-definition claim are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Pure sets are built recursively from the empty set without urelements. The proposed axioms assert empty set, extensionality, pairing, union and unrestricted comprehension; substituting non-self-membership into comprehension yields Russell's sentence, which no structure satisfies, so the theory is unsatisfiable.
samples.checks: The recursive purity condition, urelement contrast, all five axiom roles, set constructions, substitution and model-theoretic contradiction are retained.

samples.reverse_paraphrase: Mereology treats parthood as fundamental. A parthood structure interprets one binary predicate as a partial order, and every two objects have a least common whole. Additional supplementation says that an object with a proper part has a complementary disjoint part whose fusion with it is the original object.
samples.checks: The philosophical scope, proper/improper distinction, contrast with subset and membership, three partial-order axioms, fusion biconditional and final supplementation principle are retained.

source_observations: No deterministic frozen-source defect requiring a Marathi correction was found in this unit.
All formulas, macros, controlled tokens, identifiers and references match the frozen source exactly.
limitations: No independent human or native-speaker review has been performed.
The mereology, parthood, pure-set, urelement and fusion terminology remains explicitly provisional and open to specialist review in T234 through T237.
No TeX reader build was run for this individual unit.
